title: Mole Negro
subtitle: Mexican black mole sauce with dried chillies and dark chocolate
excerpt: A deeply complex sauce of dried chillies, spices, tomatoes, and dark chocolate, built in stages and simmered until completely smooth and velvety. Served over turkey or chicken, it is one of the masterpieces of Mexican cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mole negro is one of the great moles of Oaxacan cooking and one of the most complex sauces in world cuisine, involving over 30 ingredients and multiple stages of preparation. The word mole comes from the Nahuatl word molli, meaning sauce or mixture. The sauce has pre-Columbian Mesoamerican roots: the combination of chillies and cacao is ancient, and Spanish ingredients such as almonds, raisins, and spices were added after conquest. Mole negro from Oaxaca is distinguished from other moles by the use of charred chillies and tortillas, which give it its very dark colour and distinctive bitter, smoky character.

content.text: Mole negro takes time: plan for at least 2.5 hours from start to finish. The key stages are toasting the dried chillies (do this over a dry pan until fragrant but not burned), soaking them to soften, then blending to a smooth paste. Charring the tomatoes, onion, and garlic under the grill adds the roasted base note. The chocolate goes in at the end: dark chocolate with at least 70 percent cocoa, which balances the chillies rather than making the sauce sweet.

items.preparation: dried, or use mulato chilli if available

content.text: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan over medium heat for 30 to 60 seconds per side until fragrant. Do not burn. Soak in hot water for 20 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving the soaking water.

Char the onion and unpeeled garlic under a hot grill or directly over a flame for 8 to 10 minutes until charred. Peel the garlic. In a dry pan, toast the sesame seeds and almonds until golden. Fry the raisins in a little oil for 1 minute.

Put the soaked chillies, charred onion and garlic, tinned tomatoes, sesame seeds, almonds, and raisins in a blender. Add the cumin, cinnamon, and cloves. Pour in 200 ml of the chilli soaking water. Blend until very smooth.

Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a large heavy pan over medium-high heat. Add the blended mole and fry, stirring constantly, for 10 to 12 minutes until it darkens and thickens. It will spatter. Add the chicken stock and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often. Add the chocolate and stir until melted. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Brown the chicken thighs in the remaining oil in a separate pan. Add to the mole sauce. Simmer for 30 to 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Serve with rice and warm tortillas, scattered with sesame seeds.
